Real dimensions on the drawing, leaders on texts and GD&T frames, a radius on any bend, a simpler right-click menu -- and a canvas that is easier to work on.

### Dimensions
- **Dimension tool** (in the rail, next to the GD&T frame): click two points, then click where the dimension line goes. You get the extension lines, the arrowed dimension line and the value, drawn the ISO 129 way: arrows go outside when there is no room between the extension lines, and the value reads from the bottom or from the right of the sheet.
- Aligned by default (the true distance). Hold **Shift** while placing the dimension line to get a horizontal or vertical dimension (the cursor above / below the points or beside them decides). Switch later from the Inspector or the right-click menu.
- The value is the length measured on the sheet, in mm (0 to 3 decimals). Double-click it to edit it like any text -- Ø, R, tolerances. As long as the measured number is still in the text, it follows the points ("Ø50 ±0.1" stays up to date). A number typed by hand stays as typed; **Use measured value** brings the measurement back.
- Handles on both points (they snap onto other annotations) and on the dimension line (moves the line and slides the value along it; Shift moves only the line). Ends: filled arrow, open arrow, oblique stroke or dot.
- Acrobat and other viewers show the dimension as drawn.
- The v0.2.0 "Dimension" value box is gone: a text does the same, tolerances included. PDFs saved with it reopen with an equivalent text.

### Leaders on texts and GD&T frames
- **Add Leader** (right-click, Edit menu or Ctrl+K), as in CATIA: as many leaders as you need, each with its own end shape and bend points. A leader stays on the point it designates when you move the text or the frame.
- Shift makes a bend or the tip square to the previous segment; the tip is magnetic to 0 / 45 / 90 degrees and snaps onto other annotations (Alt turns snapping off).
- Other viewers show the leaders as lines.

### A radius on every bend
- Lines, arrows, polylines, polygons and leaders: right-click on a bend > **Radius** (Enter applies, Esc cancels, one button gives every bend the same radius), or **Bend radius** in the Inspector for all bends at once.
- Annoter keeps the exact arcs; other viewers draw them as smooth curves.

### Right-click menu and stacking order
- A menu with the frequent commands as icons first: cut, copy, paste, duplicate, delete; order; the line ends as icons; shape, path, align.
- **Bring Forward / Send Backward** (Ctrl+] / Ctrl+[) go one step past the next annotation that overlaps; the menu stays open to go down a pile click after click, the canvas updates at once, and the order is now kept in the saved PDF.
- The floating bar over the selection is gone (everything it offered is in the menu and the Inspector).

### On the canvas
- Handles keep the same size at every zoom.
- The start (disc) and the end (square) of a line are told apart, with a small chevron showing the direction; hovering a handle names it.
- **Alt+Click** on a pile of annotations lists them so you can pick the one you want.
- Dragging or right-clicking the selected annotation works even where another one lies on top of it.
- Polylines and polygons: Esc, right-click, double-click or Enter finishes the shape, Backspace removes the last point, and a bar shows the point count with Finish and Cancel.
- A bend point added from the end of a line goes in the middle of the segment; a selected freehand stroke is highlighted instead of boxed; the notes of a GD&T frame sit closer to the frame.

### Document properties
- File, folder, size, PDF version, pages grouped by paper format (A0-A5, Letter, ANSI...) and rotation, and the metadata. Open them with **Alt+Enter**, by clicking the document name in the top bar, or from the Inspector when nothing is selected (it also shows a short summary).

### Downloads (portable, no install, Windows 64-bit)
- **Annoter-portable.zip** (recommended) -- unzip, then run `Annoter.exe` from the folder. Fastest start; keep the whole folder together. Unzip first: running it from inside the zip makes Windows unpack everything to a temporary folder.
- **Annoter.exe** -- single self-contained file: download and double-click.

**First launch on a new PC**: the files are not code-signed, so Windows SmartScreen may show "Windows protected your PC". Click **More info**, then **Run anyway** (once per downloaded file).

Full history: https://github.com/torakce/annoter/compare/v0.2.0...v0.3.0
